key_insight: CMDS turns frozen pretrained diffusion models into coordinated multi-agent generators by learning a shared control policy that steers their reverse processes toward coherent structured outputs.
engineering_relevance: This offers a modular way to reuse existing generative models for new multi-component tasks without retraining the full system, which is attractive for scalable simulation, planning, and design workflows.
method: Treat each pretrained diffusion model as a frozen generative primitive
Formulate coordination as a stochastic optimal control problem with an assembly-level reward and a deviation penalty
Amortize the control so the same learned policy can be reused across new task instances
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful evaluation on recovering a target distribution, enforcing multiple spatial constraints with one trained control, denoising sources from degraded mixtures, and applications in maze navigation, robot planning, and human motion generation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the assembly-level reward and control cost are specified, and coordinating multiple frozen models could be sensitive to mismatch between pretrained dynamics and the target joint behavior.
paper_title: One for All, All for One: Coordinated Multi-Agent Diffusion Steering via Stochastic Optimal Control
